name: Grade 6 T3: Planning Tables and Charts
description: Planning spreadsheet vocabulary for budgets, quantities, costs, totals, charts, titles, labels, categories, and conclusions.

words.definition: Thinking ahead and organizing steps, materials, or information before starting.
words.example: The spreadsheet helped with planning a class event.

words.definition: A plan for how much money can be spent.
words.example: The class used a budget for project materials.

words.definition: How many of something are needed or counted.
words.example: The quantity column showed how many markers to buy.

words.definition: The amount of money needed to buy or do something.
words.example: The cost of one notebook was entered in the table.

words.definition: A careful guess based on the information available.
words.example: Students estimated the cost before making the final table.

words.definition: The final amount after adding values together.
words.example: The total changed when the quantity changed.

words.definition: One thing in a list, table, or plan.
words.example: Each item in the event plan had a cost.

words.definition: The supplies or resources needed for a task.
words.example: The materials list included paper, tape, and markers.

words.definition: A visual way to show data so it is easier to understand.
words.example: The chart showed the most popular activity.

words.definition: The name that tells what a chart or table is about.
words.example: The chart title explained the survey question.

words.definition: Text that names part of a chart, table, or diagram.
words.example: The axis label told what the numbers meant.

words.definition: A group or type used to organize information.
words.example: Each favorite activity was a chart category.

words.definition: A line on a chart used to show categories or numbers.
words.example: The vertical axis showed the number of students.

words.definition: The numbers or measurements used on a chart.
words.example: The chart scale counted by twos.

words.definition: A chart that uses bars to compare categories or amounts.
words.example: The bar chart compared favorite class activities.

words.definition: A group of related data used for a chart, table, or question.
words.example: The chart was created from the assigned data set.

words.definition: Something a chart or data table can help answer.
words.example: The chart answered which option was chosen most often.

words.definition: A final statement that explains what the data shows.
words.example: The conclusion said that soccer was the most popular activity.

words.definition: To look at two or more things and notice similarities or differences.
words.example: The chart made it easy to compare categories.

words.definition: To make an idea clear using words, examples, or evidence.
words.example: Students explained what the chart showed.

words.definition: A list used to make sure required parts are complete.
words.example: The chart checklist reminded students to add a title and labels.

words.definition: Clear enough for someone to understand without confusion.
words.example: Formatting made the planning table easy to read.
